status: draft: proposed in the WP0.2 migration; the owner (with Opus) decides the final lists (seed-spec-v2 Section 12)
note: Closed list of relation families: the abstract idea that may transfer, not the surface domain. Paraphrases of one relation share a family. Used for held-out-relation splits (MASTER-PLAN Section 4.2; linter rules M6 and T5).

relation_families.definition: Charge more when demand is high and less (or nothing) when it is low, so that people shift their timing.
relation_families.example: Stockholm congestion charges by time of day (D01).

relation_families.definition: Order composite identifiers by splitting them into parts and comparing the parts as numbers from left to right.
relation_families.example: Version 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.0 (C01).

relation_families.definition: Tell people, truthfully, what most others like them do, so that they move toward that norm.
relation_families.example: Tax letters saying that nine out of ten people pay on time (D02).

relation_families.definition: Small self-chosen groups share responsibility for a debt or a loss, so members choose, watch and help each other.
relation_families.example: Group microloans with joint liability (D03).

relation_families.definition: Give the few items that carry most of the total value the most frequent attention.
relation_families.example: ABC inventory counts: high-spend items weekly, the rest less often (D04).

relation_families.definition: Release on a fixed schedule; work that is not ready waits for the next release instead of moving the date.
relation_families.example: A browser release train every six weeks (D05).

relation_families.definition: Convert each raw value by trying a fixed series of types and fall back to text when none fits.
relation_families.example: A loader that tries int, float and date before keeping a string (C02).

relation_families.definition: Cutting digits off a running value at every step biases it in one direction; keep full precision and round only what is shown.
relation_families.example: A stock index that lost half its value through truncation (C03).

relation_families.definition: Assign each item to one worker by a function of the item alone, so every machine computes the same assignment without a shared table.
relation_families.example: Cache keys spread over servers by a hash of the key (C04).

relation_families.definition: Compare groups within each stratum before pooling, because pooling can reverse the comparison.
relation_families.example: Admission rates compared department by department (C05).

relation_families.definition: The more urgent a case, the shorter the time allowed before it is handled.
relation_families.example: Hospital triage colours with maximum waiting times (spec example X01).

relation_families.definition: Make the preferred choice the default, so that doing nothing leads to it while people stay free to opt out.
relation_families.example: Automatic pension enrolment with an opt-out.

relation_families.definition: Let people bind a future choice in advance, so that later temptation cannot undo it.
relation_families.example: A savings account that stays locked until a goal date.

relation_families.definition: Expose a change to a small group first and widen it only while health measures stay within limits.
relation_families.example: A canary release to 5 percent of users.

relation_families.definition: Duplicate a critical component so that one failure does not stop the service.
relation_families.example: Two independent power feeds for a server room.

relation_families.definition: Retry a failed operation after waits that grow each time, so that retries do not overload a struggling service.
relation_families.example: Exponential backoff in a network client.

relation_families.definition: Design an operation so that repeating it has the same effect as doing it once.
relation_families.example: Payment requests that carry an idempotency key.

relation_families.definition: Bring values to one canonical form before comparing or deduplicating them.
relation_families.example: Lower-casing and trimming e-mail addresses before matching.

relation_families.definition: Check an unpredictable random sample instead of everything, so that everyone stays careful at low cost.
relation_families.example: Random ticket inspections on public transport.

relation_families.definition: Match two sides by their preferences with tentative offers, so that no pair would rather leave their matches for each other.
relation_families.example: Medical residency matching.

relation_families.definition: Rotate a burden or a scarce benefit through the members in a fixed order, so that it is shared evenly over time.
relation_families.example: A weekly cleaning roster.

relation_families.definition: Allow bursts up to a budget that refills at a fixed rate, and refuse requests when the budget is empty.
relation_families.example: An API that allows 100 calls a minute with short bursts.

relation_families.definition: Keep spare capacity or stock in reserve, so that normal variation does not cause queues or shortages.
relation_families.example: Safety stock that covers late deliveries.

relation_families.definition: Use a short fixed checklist at critical moments, so that no essential step is skipped.
relation_families.example: A surgical safety checklist before the first incision.

relation_families.definition: Summarise only a moving window of recent events instead of the whole history.
relation_families.example: A rolling seven-day average of cases.

relation_families.definition: When a component fails, fall back to a reduced service that still works instead of failing completely.
relation_families.example: Showing cached results while the database is down.

relation_families.definition: Reject bad input at the boundary at once, with a clear error, instead of letting it spread.
relation_families.example: Schema validation of incoming requests.

relation_families.definition: Store the results of an expensive computation and reuse them for repeated inputs.
relation_families.example: A cache of function results keyed by the arguments.

relation_families.definition: Charge a higher unit price for each further block of consumption, so that basic use stays cheap and heavy use pays more.
relation_families.example: Water tariffs with rising prices per block of cubic metres.

relation_families.definition: Allocate a scarce good by a fair random draw when demand exceeds supply and no merit ranking is fair.
relation_families.example: A lottery for oversubscribed school places.

relation_families.definition: Show people timely feedback about their own behaviour, so that they can adjust it.
relation_families.example: A smart meter display of the day's electricity use.

relation_families.definition: Break ties by a fixed secondary key, so that the order is the same on every run.
relation_families.example: Sorting by score and then by ID.
